sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Policy of Continuity**: Jahangir largely maintained Akbar's administrative structure but shifted focus from aggressive expansion to **consolidation** and internal stability.
• **Deccan Stalemate**: The Deccan policy shifted from total annexation to a **tributary/buffer state** model, acknowledging the difficulty of controlling the rugged terrain.
• **Kandahar Geopolitics**: The loss of **Kandahar (1622)** to the Safavids marked a significant strategic setback, exposing the vulnerability of the North-Western frontier.
• **Key Metric**: The **Mansabdari system** was refined with the introduction of **Du-Aspa Sih-Aspa** to increase military efficiency without increasing the number of mansabdars.

The guerrilla warfare tactics employed by Malik Ambar in the Deccan, which severely hampered Mughal territorial expansion.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Diplomatic Consolidation**: Use of matrimonial alliances and honorary titles to pacify Rajput states.
• **Frontier Management**: Heavy reliance on the Kabul-Kandahar axis to prevent Persian and Central Asian incursions.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The rise of the Maratha power in the Deccan and the loss of the strategic Kandahar fortress.
• **Solutions**: Increased focus on the 'Zat' and 'Sawar' classification to ensure better fiscal control over the Jagirdari system.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-M-K' (Kangra, Mewar, Kandahar).
• **Decoded Meaning**: K(angra 1620) - M(ewar 1615) - K(andahar 1622). These are the three pillars of Jahangir's territorial narrative.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Treaty of Chittor' (1615) with the 'Annexation of Mewar'. Jahangir did NOT annex Mewar; he allowed the Rana to retain his ancestral lands in exchange for nominal vassalage.

Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Strategic Depth' when discussing the loss of Kandahar. It highlights the shift from a secure frontier to a vulnerable one, leading to the eventual decline of Mughal influence in Central Asia.

keyTakeaways: Jahangir prioritized consolidation over the rapid expansionism of Akbar.
The loss of Kandahar in 1622 was a turning point in Mughal foreign policy.
The Deccan remained the 'graveyard' of Mughal resources due to the effective guerrilla tactics of Malik Ambar.
